sections.label: Beneficial ownership transparency framework
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Minister for Law prescribe regulations on beneficial ownership and identity information for trusts, following FATF recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In September 2016, the National Steering Committee for Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing announced that Singapore will follow up on certain areas of improvement recommended by the FATF assessors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This included enhancing the transparency on beneficial ownership of companies, limited liability partnerships and trusts, and ensuring that such information is more readily accessible to law enforcement agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To this end, the Bill introduces a framework for the Minister for Law to prescribe the necessary regulations, so as to give effect to the FATF recommendations and GF requirements concerning beneficial ownership and identity information and/or the keeping of accounting records in relation to trusts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Similar amendments were introduced in respect of companies and limited liability partnerships (LLPs) by way of the Companies (Amendment) Bill and the LLPs (Amendment) Bill which were passed in this House earlier today.

sections.label: Fines for regulation breaches
sections.summary: The amendments empower the Minister to prescribe breaches of regulations as offences punishable by a maximum fine of $1,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To discourage the breach of regulations, the proposed amendments empower the Minister to prescribe breaches of the regulations as offences punishable by way of a fine.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Having regard to the comparative severity of the existing sanctions under the Trustees Act in respect of other offences, the maximum fine for such breaches is $1,000, which is a proportionate sanction for the purposes of Part VII.

sections.label: Penalties for trust companies
sections.summary: Breach of regulatory notices may make trust companies liable for a fine not exceeding $1 million, part of efforts against financial crime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Breach of such regulatory notices may render trust companies liable for an offence punishable by way of a fine not exceeding $1 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To sum up, the amendments contemplated are part of a concerted effort to ensure that legal entities, such as companies and LLPs, as well as legal arrangements, such as trusts, do not readily lend themselves to financial crime.

sections.label: Trustees' beneficial ownership obligations
sections.summary: The report highlighted the lack of enforceable obligations on trustees to collect beneficial ownership information beyond the immediate beneficiary.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The report specifically highlighted the lack of enforceable obligations on trustees to collect beneficial ownership information relating to a trust beyond the immediate beneficiary.

sections.label: Indonesian amnesty overseas funds
sections.summary: The Indonesian amnesty on overseas funds revealed $72.4 billion in private bank accounts in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year also saw the Indonesian amnesty on overseas funds which revealed that $72.4 billion was sitting in private bank accounts on our shores.

sections.label: Central registry of trusts
sections.summary: Section 84A(2)(g) allows a fine of up to $1,000, and the question asks if a central registry of Singapore-connected trusts was considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 84A(2)(g) provides that we may impose a fine of up to $1,000 for non-compliance with regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To ensure that investigators will have ready access to the necessary information, has the Ministry considered the viability of setting up a central registry of all trusts that have connections to Singapore?

sections.label: Fine amount and trusts registry
sections.summary: The Ministry assessed a fine not exceeding $1,000 as proportionate, and has no plans for a central registry of Singapore-connected trusts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In the circumstances, my Ministry assessed that a fine not exceeding $1,000 would be appropriate as it balances the need for deterrence with the need for a proportionate sanction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Second, Mr Louis Ng asked if the Ministry has considered the viability of setting up a central registry of all trusts that have connections to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have considered the issue but, at present, have no plans to set up such a registry.

sections.label: Trustee fraud and statutory duty
sections.summary: Trustees who commit fraud or criminal breach of trust can be prosecuted, and no trend indicates a need to criminalise breaches of statutory duty of care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Where a trustee acts so egregiously to commit fraud or criminal breach of trust, he or she can be prosecuted under the criminal law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have not seen any trend or development indicating a need to criminalise breaches of a trustee's statutory duty of care.

sections.label: Accountants Act amendments after Companies Bill
sections.summary: Consequential amendments to the Accountants Act will be made after the Companies (Amendment) Bill to give more bite to rules for public accountants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Following the Companies (Amendment) Bill, which has just been passed by this House, consequential and related amendments to the Accountants Act will be made to give more bite to the applicable rules and standards for public accountants, including EP 200.
